stories.title: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
stories.summary: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting the Bricksforge plugin for WordPress has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to Patchstack. The critical vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-85097 (CVSS score: 10.0), which allows unauthenticated attackers to upload and execute arbitrary PHP code on vulnerable WordPress websites, resulting in remote code execution (RCE). The
stories.explanation: A WordPress plugin called Bricksforge has a severe flaw (rated 10.0 out of 10 in severity) that lets attackers who aren't logged in upload and run malicious code on websites using it. This matters because WordPress powers millions of websites, and attackers are actively using this flaw right now to compromise sites. Defenders need to update the Bricksforge plugin immediately, monitor for suspicious file uploads, and check their sites for signs of compromise.

stories.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
stories.summary: The vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-85097 can allow threat actors to take control of the targeted WordPress websites.
stories.explanation: The same Bricksforge vulnerability allows attackers to take complete control of affected WordPress websites without needing legitimate access. This is critical because a compromised website can be used to steal customer data, spread malware, or damage the organization's reputation. Defenders should prioritize patching all instances of this plugin and consider disabling it temporarily if updates aren't available.

stories.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records
stories.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a two-pronged artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented initial access campaign targeting WordPress sites, e-commerce platforms, and critical infrastructure entities in Ukraine. The activity, which brings together commodity offensive tools like Cobalt Strike with an AI orchestration layer powered by Anthropic's Claude Code, has been attributed
stories.explanation: A group called CyberXero used AI-powered tools to launch coordinated attacks against WordPress sites, online stores, and critical infrastructure in Ukraine, stealing information on over 628,000 people. This matters because it shows attackers are combining AI capabilities with traditional hacking tools to be more effective at scale. Defenders should strengthen access controls, monitor for unusual upload activity, and implement multi-factor authentication to make initial compromise harder.

stories.title: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaw Targeted in 135 Exploitation Attempts After Patch
stories.summary: Threat actors have been observed exploiting a recently disclosed critical security flaw in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 appliances within days of public disclosure. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of pre-authenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) that could allow a remote attacker "to direct the appliance to issue requests on their
stories.explanation: A critical flaw in SonicWall's mobile access appliances (CVE-2026-102255) is being actively exploited within days of becoming public; attackers can trick the device into making unauthorized requests to other systems even without logging in first. This matters because these appliances often protect remote worker access to corporate networks, so compromise could expose entire organizations. Defenders must apply security patches urgently, limit who can access these devices from the internet, and monitor network traffic for suspicious outbound requests.

stories.title: Ransomware Response Expert Arrested in ShinyHunters FBI Hack Probe
stories.summary: The suspect is believed to be Edward Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity executive who was visiting the United States for a conference.
stories.explanation: A suspect arrested in connection with a major cybersecurity hack targeting ShinyHunters is reportedly Edward Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity expert, suggesting insider knowledge may have been involved in the attack. This matters because it highlights that threats can come from people with legitimate security expertise who turn to crime. Defenders should implement background checks, monitor privileged user behavior closely, and separate access duties so no single person can compromise critical systems alone.

stories.title: iRhythm Data Breach Impacts at Least 360,000 People
stories.summary: Hackers stole patients’ personal information, including names, addresses, email addresses, dates of birth, and phone numbers.
stories.explanation: Hackers broke into iRhythm and stole personal information from at least 360,000 patients, including names, addresses, emails, birthdates, and phone numbers. This matters because stolen personal data can be used for identity theft, phishing scams, and sold to other criminals. Defenders should encrypt sensitive data at rest, limit who can access it, and establish a process to notify affected people and offer credit monitoring services.

stories.title: Critical SonicWall Vulnerability Exploited Days After Disclosure
stories.summary: CVE-2026-102255 is a pre-authenticated SSRF flaw that could allow attackers to perform unauthorized operations.
stories.explanation: The SonicWall flaw CVE-2026-102255 is a pre-authenticated SSRF (server-side request forgery) vulnerability, meaning attackers can make the device request unauthorized information from internal systems without logging in. This matters because internal systems often have weaker security than the device facing the internet, so this could be a stepping stone to deeper network compromise. Defenders should block internet access to these devices where possible, use firewalls to restrict what traffic they can send internally, and monitor logs for unusual requests.

stories.title: Ledger Finds Unauthorized Hardware Implant in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallet Amid Fund Theft Reports
stories.summary: Cryptocurrency hardware maker Ledger has temporarily paused sales of its products via Cryptobilis following reports of stolen funds linked to devices sold by the reseller. On Friday, the company said it was investigating reports of loss of funds from users in Southeast Asia who had purchased products from CryptoBilis. The incident is said to have resulted in losses totaling more than $86
stories.explanation: Ledger, a cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker, found unauthorized hardware modifications in devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis and paused sales after reports of stolen funds from Southeast Asian customers. This matters because if attackers physically modify hardware before it reaches customers, they can steal cryptocurrency even from devices designed to be secure. Defenders (in this case Ledger) should verify the integrity of hardware before shipment, work only with trusted resellers, and investigate supply chain security.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-5477 is a data processing error in ISC BIND (the most common DNS software), allowing attackers to cause denial of service (crash the DNS service) or potentially execute code. This matters because DNS is critical infrastructure—if DNS stops working, websites and email become unreachable. Defenders should keep BIND updated with security patches and deploy redundancy so one compromised DNS server doesn't take down service.

cves.explanation: CVE-2015-3306 is an access control flaw in ProFTPD (file transfer software) that lets attackers bypass authentication checks and access files they shouldn't. This matters because FTP is often used to manage website and application files, so this flaw could lead to unauthorized file uploads or downloads. Defenders should update ProFTPD, disable FTP if not needed, use SFTP (a more secure alternative) instead, and monitor file access logs.

cves.explanation: CVE-2016-3081 is a command injection vulnerability in Apache Struts (a web framework), allowing attackers to run arbitrary system commands through specially crafted input. This matters because web frameworks run the core logic of many applications, so this flaw could lead to full system compromise. Defenders should patch Struts immediately, validate all user input before processing, and use security tools to detect injection attack attempts.

cves.explanation: CVE-2021-3199 is a path traversal flaw in ONLYOFFICE Docs Server that lets attackers read files from anywhere on the system by manipulating file paths in requests. This matters because ONLYOFFICE often stores sensitive documents and configuration files on the same server, so this could expose passwords, database credentials, and private data. Defenders should patch the software, restrict file system permissions, and monitor for suspicious file access patterns.

cves.name: Strapi Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2023-22894 in Strapi (a headless CMS platform) stores sensitive information like API keys in plain text instead of encrypted, making them easy for attackers to steal if they gain file access. This matters because API keys grant access to connect and control systems, so exposed keys are equivalent to stolen passwords. Defenders should encrypt sensitive configuration data, rotate compromised API keys immediately, and implement code reviews to catch this type of storage mistake before deployment.
